title: Replace combinational division with a radix-4 iterative unit
motivation:
The baseline's 199.837 ns worst path passes through the EX ALU, whose
combinational 32-bit divide and remainder operators dominate logic depth.
That sets Fmax to 5.442 MHz even when CoreMark executes no divide in a
given cycle. A compact iterative divider trades latency on rare divide
instructions for a much shorter clock period on every instruction.

hypothesis.motivation:
The baseline's 199.837 ns worst path passes through the EX ALU, whose

That sets Fmax to 5.442 MHz even when CoreMark executes no divide in a

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace all DIV, DIVU, REM, and REMU combinational operators with one
shared radix-4 unsigned restoring divider that resolves two quotient bits
per cycle, at most 16 iterations. Convert signed operands to magnitudes
on launch and correct quotient/remainder signs on completion. Handle
divide-by-zero and INT_MIN/-1 exactly as RV32M specifies. Interlock EX
while the divider runs: hold IF and ID/EX, let older instructions drain,
insert bubbles into EX/MEM, and emit the division result exactly once
when ready. Preserve the ALTOPS stand-ins in formal mode. The real-mode
interval from the previous retirement through a division retirement
must remain within the existing 20-cycle liveness bound. The expected
Fmax improvement should outweigh the extra CoreMark divide cycles.

changes.description: Remove the real-mode combinational divide and remainder data paths while preserving the exact ALTOPS expressions and all other ALU operations.
Add a shared radix-4 sequential quotient/remainder unit with signed pre/post processing, RV32M corner cases, and a one-result handshake.
Launch division with forwarded operands, select its result for EX/MEM, and inject EX/MEM bubbles while it runs without repeating side effects or losing forwarding data.
Connect divider busy/done state to the pipeline interlock and preserve the existing single-channel RVFI port and retirement order.
Coordinate divide holds with load-use, imem backpressure, dmem backpressure, and redirect priority while allowing older instructions to drain.
Exercise the sequential divider handshake and exact results of all eight RV32M operations, including signs, zero divisors, and overflow.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-001-r1s0 (improvement, +793.32%): Replacing the combinational RV32M DIV/REM path in EX with a shared 16-cycle radix-4 divider shortens the clock path enough to outweigh divide stalls in CoreMark.

title: Move division off the single-cycle execute path
motivation:
The baseline reaches only 5.442 MHz, and its 156-cell critical path runs
from MEM/WB forwarding through EX arithmetic toward the data-memory port.
The combinational RV32M quotient and remainder operators force a full
32-bit divide network into this one-cycle EX path, while also contributing
substantial logic to the 12,312-LUT design. CoreMark should benefit more
from a shorter common EX path than it loses to the latency of infrequent
DIV and REM instructions.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Replace the synthesized combinational DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU datapath in the
production core with one shared, 16-step radix-4 restoring divider. Keep the
instruction in EX while the divider runs; let older MEM and WB operations
drain, inject bubbles into EX/MEM, and retire the divide exactly once when
its registered result is ready. Handle signed quotient/remainder correction,
divide by zero, and INT_MIN / -1 explicitly. Preserve the combinational
ALU unit-test interface and the existing RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS behavior via
a constant ALU parameter: direct ALU tests use combinational division,
while the core disables it and takes divide results from the iterative
unit. Complete division and retirement within the formal suite's 20-cycle
liveness window. This should substantially raise Fmax and reduce LUT use
at a modest CoreMark cycle cost.

title: Fetch-stage direct-branch prediction with a small history table
motivation:
The current core resolves every taken branch and JAL in EX, then discards
the younger instruction being fetched in that cycle. CoreMark repeatedly
executes loop and decision branches, so this branch bubble recurs throughout
the timed region. The measured critical path is through the M-extension ALU,
leaving room for a compact predictor without targeting that path.

hypothesis.motivation:
The current core resolves every taken branch and JAL in EX, then discards
the younger instruction being fetched in that cycle. CoreMark repeatedly
executes loop and decision branches, so this branch bubble recurs throughout
the timed region. The measured critical path is through the M-extension ALU,
leaving room for a compact predictor without targeting that path.
hypothesis.hypothesis:
Predict direct control flow in IF: JAL is always taken, and a 128-entry
two-bit saturating branch history table predicts conditional branches.
Untrained entries use backward-taken/forward-not-taken as the cold-start
direction. Form the B/J immediate and predicted next PC from the fetched
instruction; advance the PC to that address only when the instruction bus
is ready and the existing pipeline stall rules allow it. Carry the predicted
next PC with the instruction through ID/EX. Never predict a misaligned
direct target, which will trap in EX. In EX, compare the prediction with the
resolved next PC and redirect/flush only on a mismatch, including a
misaligned-target trap; train the table once when a valid branch advances
from EX. Keep JALR on the existing resolve path. This should remove the
normal one-cycle penalty for taken JALs and correctly predicted branches
while preserving the exact retirement and RVFI behavior.

changes.description: Add predicted-next-PC metadata to the IF/ID and ID/EX bundles.
Decode direct branch/JAL targets during fetch, consult and train a small two-bit direction table, and select the predicted PC under existing stalls.
Carry the fetch prediction into ID/EX without altering decode or retirement.
Compare predicted and actual next PC, redirect only on a valid misprediction, and expose one branch-training event per advancing branch.
Connect branch prediction metadata and EX training to IF, and gate correction during a held EX stage.
Flush the younger instructions only on an EX misprediction while retaining load-use and bus-stall priority.
Check taken and untaken branches, JAL, cold-start direction, misprediction recovery, and stalls without changing the existing invariant checks.

lesson: - 2026-09-29 hyp-20260929-003-r1s2 (regression, +5.53%): A 128-entry IF branch history table yields only a modest CoreMark gain while the combinational RV32M EX path still limits clock speed, so branch-bubble savings cannot match shortening that path.
